messages:
maria: Heads-up — a customer hit a silent fallback from v2 -> v1 yesterday; their throughput spiked and billing alerts fired but console showed no banner or attribution. They only noticed because latency regressed. Thinking we need a two-part change: (1) detect and surface silent fallbacks per-route in the console, (2) add telemetry that ties fallback events to quota/billing deltas. @aj @kate any quick wins?

aj: ugh. Do we have a reliable signal currently? we log route_routed_to and model_variant but fallbacks can happen in the proxy layer as a transient. if proxy emits fallback=true in request logs we can wire that, but need a matching product surface.

maria: proxy does emit, but it's at debug level and not linked to tenant_id in the same event sometimes (sampling). customer had a quota spike because v1 token cost > v2 for their seqlen mix.

kate: short term: console can show a "compat fallback" toast per-route when fallback rate > 0.5% over 5m. include a link to a new telemetry view showing fallback_rate vs token_delta. longer term: surface cost delta and option to pin route to preferred variant.

ravi: for telemetry: emit a new metric fallback_count{route,tenant,from_variant,to_variant} and fallback_token_delta{tenant,route} as aggregates. we can roll that into per-tenant billing signals. low-cost: populate a detective dashboard in grafana first.

aj: agreed on metric names. also suggest a probe that runs at console-level: simulate header negotiation and verify route affinity. something like:
```
curl -H 'x-client-version: 2' -H 'x-tenant: T-123' https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# expect: route=routing-v2 pool, variant=v2; if fallback=true -> emit alert
```

maria: love the probe. UX: deploy a small console affordance "show recent fallbacks" in route detail with a quick toggle: [pin to preferred variant]. pin should create a tenant-scoped override that prevents automatic fallback for 24h and surface cost warning.

kate: careful: pinning can break reliability guarantees. we need guardrails: pin only allowed for tenants on dedicated/dedicated-like tiers, or require explicit owner consent modal that warns about failed requests on overload.

ravi: +1. implement policy -> pin_request -> policy_service checks tenant_tier; if denied return 403 with reason. also we should emit audit log entry.

aj: rollout plan: (0) add fallback metric (counter) and fallback_token_delta. (1) wire sample logs to include tenant consistently. (2) add console badge and grafana dashboard. (3) soft-launch pin toggle behind feature flag for internal tenants. (4) run a 2-week canary, measure error-rate delta.

maria: timeline? can we get (0)-(2) in 2 sprints? ops needs the metric to prevent future billing surprises.

aj: metric + sampling changes = 1 sprint infra work. console badge + simple grafana = next sprint. pin behind flag = optional stretch.

kate: UX copy for the badge: "Automatic fallback to compatible model detected — may affect cost and latency. [View details] [Pin preferred variant]". include a link to cost projection (token delta * recent traffic).

ravi: runbook snippet to include in incident response: detect sudden increase in fallback_token_delta > threshold -> notify oncall + post to #incidents with tenant link + suggested mitigation (pin or increase capacity).

maria: ok. action items: @aj add metric ticket and sampling change. @ravi create grafana panels & runbook PR. @kate draft badge copy and modal flows. I'll coordinate canary tenants and stakeholder comms.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/metrics-fallback -> staging (started)

aj: thanks — I'll post PRs in eng-platform and tag you all. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone. Let's aim for a staging roll by end of next week and internal canary the week after.
